symptom: After the mendixlabs/mxcli#1489 splice (activity with a custom error handler swapped in place), `create or modify` adding `@annotation 'calls the sub'` to such a call reported 'Modified … (spliced)' but the note was not written; rewording the call's note was refused
cause: keepStoredHandler stripped the replacement fragment to its entry activity alone so the stored handler would be kept — which also stripped the note objects and lines the builder drew for the statement's own @annotation. handlerEdit refused replaceNotes outright for the same reason
fix: keepStoredHandler keeps the entry plus the notes linked to it and their lines; replaceKeepingHandler splits them off (withoutNotes), swaps the activity in place, translates unpinned notes by the activity's move from builder to stored position, and appends them. handlerEdit passes ReplaceNotes, so the stored notes are removed first and the stated ones written
test: mdl/executor/flow_splice_error_handler_pedapp_test.go subtests 'note added to the call' (1 replaced + 1 added, describe shows it, re-run Unchanged) and 'note on the call reworded'. With the two source files reverted both fail: describe lacks the note
insight: A fragment trimmed to 'just the activity' must say what else the statement owns: notes are separate nodes with their own lines, so any fragment surgery that keeps one object drops them silently while the run reports success. The canon write elision then hid it further — the swapped activity equal to the stored one carried the stored $ID, so the run looked like nothing happened rather than like a loss
